steps.domain_action: Initialize the system with the integer N to be factored and define the factor base B.
Establish the self-referential polynomial pair (f, g) that maps Z to the number field K.
Begin the forward sieving process, generating candidate integers from the lattice.
Split each candidate into its rational norm and algebraic norm components.
Check the rational norm for B-smoothness; if smooth, proceed.
Check the algebraic norm for B-smoothness; if not smooth, reject.
Hold the state where one side is smooth and the other is not, maintaining the paradox until resolution.
Record the relation if both sides are smooth, appending to the permanent relation log.
Backtrack if the relation is invalid, returning to the lattice search without consuming resources.
Compose the collected smooth relations into the large sparse exponent matrix.
Perform linear algebra (e.g., Lanczos or Wiedemann) to find a linear dependency in the matrix.
Fuse the dependency vector into a congruence of squares a^2 ≡ b^2 (mod n).
Verify that gcd(a-b, n) yields a non-trivial factor.
Seal the system with the extracted factor, completing the factorization.
